messages.subject: naive position_beeswarm() implementation
parts:
I forked ggplot2 to toy with implementing a position_beeswarm, based off position_jitter; though various recipes for using beeswarm to pre-process data exist, I wanted an embedded ggplot solution that would work with faceting, etc.

The first hurdle I encountered was one of size/cex: to properly reposition each point, beeswarm needs to know how big the points are going to be drawn (it get's this from par("cex") in the context of base graphics), but position_* manipulations occur independently.  As a workaround, I added an "extra" variable to pass along hints to beeswarm so that the user can adjust cex (and perhaps other things like spacing, etc).

You can try it out this way:

library(devtools)
install_github("ggplot2", username="amackey")
library(ggplot2)

# with jitter: hard to see overlaps/distribution, and not centered:
qplot(Species, Sepal.Length, data=iris, position=position_jitter(width=0.05, height=0))
# with beeswarm:
qplot(Species, Sepal.Length, data=iris, position=position_beeswarm(method="hex"))
# or spaced out a bit more:
qplot(Species, Sepal.Length, data=iris, position=position_beeswarm(method="hex", extra=list(cex=5)))

There are lots of other problems (e.g. for this particular qplot, method="swarm" doesn't work though it does work with some of my own datasets), but I wanted to get this out there so that someone with better "chops" can run with it faster than I can.

-Aaron
